meta.note: A snapshot of the Pokémon TCG card-image ecosystem. Links marked verified are pixel matches; the rest are the sites' own statements or indirect evidence. Not legal advice.

official.label: Official Pokémon
official.desc: The Pokémon Company, its regional companies and its game clients. The only true origin of digital card images.

extract.label: Game-client extract
extract.desc: Renders pulled out of the official game clients and re-published.

dataset.label: Scraped dataset
dataset.desc: A dump of an official source, published as a dataset.

rehost.label: Fan database / API
rehost.desc: Card databases and APIs. Mostly re-host digital images from upstream sources.

wiki.label: Fan wiki
wiki.desc: Community wikis. Modern cards re-hosted, vintage cards uploaded by users.

scan.label: Scan / photo source
scan.desc: Images made by scanning or photographing physical cards. Owned by whoever scanned them.

market.label: Marketplace / tracker
market.desc: Shops, price guides and collection trackers.

tcgdex.label: TCGdex
tcgdex.desc: The open card database this atlas centres on.

print.label: Printed cards
print.desc: Physical cards. The origin of every scan and photo.

sources.name: Printed cards
sources.origin: Physical cards. The origin of every scan and photo. For Western cards from Base Set to Platinum (1999–2010), and Japanese cards before 2006, no official digital image was ever published online, so every picture of those cards is somebody's scan or photo.

sources.name: Pokémon TCG Online (game client)
sources.eras: HGSS (2010) → Sword & Shield (2023), plus promos and trainer kits
sources.origin: The Pokémon Company's own digital card renders, shipped inside the Pokémon TCG Online client (retired 2023).

sources.name: Pokémon TCG Live (game client)
sources.eras: Scarlet & Violet (2023) → Mega Evolution, plus promos
sources.origin: TPC's own digital card renders, shipped inside the game client.

sources.name: pokemon-card.com (Japan)
sources.origin: The Pokémon Company's official Japanese card database. Stops at the last regular number: SM/early-SwSh secret-rare tails and M6a 104–135 are not listed. Nothing before DP (2006).

sources.name: asia.pokemon-card.com (tw · th · id · sg · hk)

sources.origin: The Pokémon Company's official Asian card databases. The Singapore site carries the international English print at 744×1040, larger than TCGdex's 600×825 English images.

sources.name: pokemon.com card database
sources.origin: TPC International's official Western card search. Useful only as a witness: the images are too small.

sources.name: pokemoncard.co.kr (Pokémon Korea)
sources.origin: The official Korean card database. Its image server hands out only watermarked images ("Pokémon Card Game" across the card).

terms.summary: No licence. Asks for a credit on your credits page ("not a legal or licensing requirement").

sources.origin: Publishes the card renders from the Pokémon TCG Online and TCG Live game clients. The main public source of clean Western digital card images from HGSS (2010) on: TCGdex, pokemontcg.io, pkmncards, TCGplayer, TCG Collector and the wikis all carry files identical to its exports.

sources.name: Pokémon Paradijs scans (Martin)

terms.summary: Martin's own scans; no licence published. pkmncards.com credits "Martin of Pokémon Paradijs" for most of its pre-HGSS images.

sources.origin: Martin of Pokémon Paradijs scanned almost the entire English vintage era (Base Set → Platinum) in consistent, high quality. Those scans are the backbone of English vintage images on the web: pkmncards, pokemontcg.io, Scrydex, TCGdex, TCGplayer and TCG Collector all serve the same files. Remarkable work that deserves a credit wherever it's used.

terms.summary: All rights reserved, no reuse licence. Under German law scans and photos may be protected in their own right (§72 UrhG, Lichtbildschutz).

api.note: The site's own JSON API is undocumented. Automated and AI clients must follow its access policy (/ai-access.json).

terms.summary: Footer: card text and images © The Pokémon Company, Pokémon Shanghai, Nintendo, Game Freak, Creatures; all data comes from Pokémon Shanghai; used only for non-commercial, academic and research purposes. Automated or AI access must identify itself truthfully and state its purpose on every request; robots.txt asks for 10 s between requests.

sources.origin: A Simplified Chinese competitive-play site (card search, deck and tournament statistics). Its footer says all data comes from Pokémon Shanghai. Its card images are pixel-identical to the duanxr dataset's (7 of 7 sampled, re-encoded PNGs), i.e. the WeChat app's. It shows one image per card number (the dataset also keeps holo variants) and groups boxes into sets; in the sets we compared we found no card the dataset lacks, and nothing larger than 300×419.

sources.origin: One file per card, filed under every printing. Its Japanese-set categories are mostly pokemon-card.com's official Japanese images (2,419 pixel copies), plus malie renders (316). The Japanese secret rares are credited "From Pokeca.net" and carry pokeca.net's watermark.

sources.name: TCGdex

submissions.how: Images via the Ingest upload page (manager.tcgdex.net/ingest); card data via GitHub pull requests (CONTRIBUTING rejects AI-assisted data PRs)

terms.summary: Card data MIT-licensed. Image sources aren't listed per card. Takes image uploads through its Ingest page.

sources.origin: By pixel match: HGSS → Mega Evolution Pitch Black (me05) in every Western language is the exact same files as the game-client renders malie published (often months earlier). Pixels can't tell whether TCGdex took them from malie or from the game directly. The newest set, 30th Celebration (Sep 2026), is different: a differently cropped render that isn't malie's file and was online about 5 hours before malie's export, so it came from another source. English 1999–2010 is 98–99% Martin's Pokémon Paradijs scans. French vintage shares 50–73% of its files with pkmcards.fr. No German before HGSS. Sampled zh-cn images are the Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) print.

callouts.title: Korean: official images are watermarked
callouts.body: Pokémon Korea's official site (pokemoncard.co.kr) is the only digital source, and it serves only watermarked images. Every Korean fan database we found links to those same files. PriceCharting's Korean images are mostly photos of real cards (no watermark, but glare and texture), plus some official watermarked ones. No clean digital Korean image found anywhere (2010 → today).

callouts.title: Simplified Chinese: only the WeChat app, only 300×419
callouts.body: The only official source is Pokémon Shanghai's WeChat mini-program. Its images were scraped into the GitHub dataset duanxr/PTCG-CHS-Datasets at the app's native 300×419; we found nothing larger. AREAZERO.GG (tcg.mik.moe) shows the same images (pixel-identical in our sample) and no extra cards in the sets we compared. The dataset forbids redistribution without Pokémon Shanghai's written consent. Sampled TCGdex zh-cn images are the Traditional Chinese (Taiwan) print.

callouts.title: Better quality exists than TCGdex serves
callouts.body: TCGdex serves 600×825. malie's originals are 734×1024 with transparent corners; the Singapore English print on asia.pokemon-card.com is 744×1040; TCG Collector's Japanese scans reach 1280×1788; bisafans' German vintage photos are ≈ 860×1200.

callouts.title: Western 1999–2010 has no official digital image
callouts.body: No Base Set → Platinum card was ever published as an official digital image online. Every image of those cards, TCGdex's included, is somebody's scan. For English, nearly everyone uses the same scans by Martin of Pokémon Paradijs.
